## jig v0.2.0-alpha.1

The first published jig release. Channels can be end-to-end encrypted with MLS, and every
restricted channel and DM is. Servers are untrusted by design; see the
[threat register](https://github.com/jig-protocol/jig/blob/main/repos/jig-spec/src/threat-register.md).

This is an alpha. Pre-1.0 releases make no wire, receipt or storage compatibility guarantee, and
jig has not had an external security audit yet (D27).

### Breaking changes

- **Restricted channels are always MLS (D25).** Creating a restricted channel without MLS is
  refused with `RESTRICTED_REQUIRES_MLS`. Restricted channels created in plaintext before this
  release are frozen: their history stays readable (in plaintext, to the operator too), new
  content is refused with `CHANNEL_FROZEN`, and promoting one to open lets it take content again.
  `jig channel create --visibility restricted` makes an MLS channel with no flag; `--encrypted`
  stays and still selects MLS for open channels.
- **The email bridge refuses inbound mail** until it can join channels as an MLS member. Mail
  threads are restricted channels, and the server no longer accepts them in plaintext. Existing
  mail threads are frozen like any other plaintext restricted channel.
- **The v0.0.1 `POST /blocks` route is removed (D28)**, together with its
  `dangerously_enable_v0_0_1_rest` flag. Unsigned v0.0.1 submissions have no route.
- **The `/_admin_v0_0_2` route aliases are removed.** `debug.admin_endpoints` no longer does
  anything; a config that still sets it loads and the key is ignored.
- **The nameserver's legacy v0.0.1 HTTP routes are removed**, with their proof-of-work and
  claim-signature modules. Only the v0.0.2 routes remain.
- **Runtime pricing config is strict.** `[pricing]` rejects unknown keys, and
  `schedule_version` can no longer be set: a config that sets it fails to load, so delete the
  line.
- **Receipts sign the engine identity.** The signed `0.3-render` receipt payload carries
  `engine.identity` (the exact wasmtime version, an engine configuration fingerprint and the fuel
  schedule) in place of `runtime_version`. Receipts from earlier builds do not have it.
- **The CLI's default server URL is `https://127.0.0.1:7117`.** Servers serve TLS by default as
  of this release; a plaintext server needs an explicit `http://` URL.
- **Blocks whose clock runs too far ahead are refused** with `CLOCK_SKEW`. The server signs the
  bound in its welcome.

### What's new

- **MLS per channel** (RFC 9420, `openmls`). The server validates commits as a delivery service
  and holds no group secret. `jig channel create --encrypted`, and every `jig dm`.
- **Restricted channels are always MLS** (D25). There is no plaintext restricted channel; a
  creator who wants plaintext makes an open channel.
- **Channel dynamics**: `member-remove` (kick and leave) and owner-signed membership changes.
- **TLS on by default**: the server makes its own certificate, its DID vouches for it, and
  clients trust it through the DID they pin. TLS 1.3 only.
- **Pinning**: clients pin a server's DID from its signed welcome and a channel's suite from its
  signed creation block, and refuse a server or channel that later claims otherwise.
- **Handshake**: refusals are signed and name their format, connections close with a stated
  class, and the client checks later frames against the welcome.
- **Federation through the write gate**: relayed blocks are ingested like local ones; peers are
  pinned and listed. Federation fails closed: a relayed post for a channel this server never saw
  created is refused, not stored.
- **Admission limits**: per-DID and per-address rate limits, and optional proof-of-work for DIDs
  a server has not seen. The nameserver rate-limits `register`, `rotate` and `renew`.
- **Wasm determinism**: modules are checked against a feature allowlist before they run, and the
  engine enables only the features that allowlist accepts.
- **Key files are created owner-only** by the server and the nameserver.
- **Installer**: `install.sh` verifies the signed `SHA256SUMS` and the tarball checksum, and
  refuses to install when it cannot check the signature (`JIG_VERIFY_SIGNATURE=0` to override).

### Known limitations

- **A channel federates only if a peer saw its `channel-create`**: created after the two servers
  peered and while their link was up. Relayed posts to any other channel are refused, not stored
  as orphans. A later release (F2's `contract-offer`) closes this.
- **Identity keys are not encrypted at rest.** The CLI stores each identity key unencrypted
  (owner-only) under `~/.jig/keys/`. Sealing it with the OS keychain or a passphrase comes in a
  later release.
- **History is not yet sequenced by the server.** Signed per-channel ingest records, and the
  client check that history matches the chain it pinned, are not in this release. History is
  still ordered by the authors' clocks (TM-02, OP-06).

### Threat-register entries mitigated

Statuses are as of this release. *Partial* means part of the entry's decision is implemented;
the register says which part.

| Entry | What this release does | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OP-01 Stripped handshake | WSS refuses any frame before `hello`; the client closes on a missing or malformed welcome; closes carry a stated class | Partial |
| OP-02 False handshake answers | The welcome and refusals are signed; the client pins the welcome's DID and suites and checks later frames against the welcome | Partial |
| OP-03 Suite downgrade | A channel's suite is fixed at creation and enforced on every post; the client pins it from the signed creation block | Partial |
| OP-05 Content disclosure | Restricted channels and DMs are end-to-end encrypted (MLS) and the server stores ciphertext; a plaintext restricted channel is refused. Restricted channels created in plaintext earlier are frozen, with their history still readable by the operator. Open channels are plaintext unless created MLS | Partial |
| OP-08 Key substitution | The CLI pins each server's DID and accepts only the TLS certificate that DID vouches for. A name's DID is not yet pinned | Partial |
| OP-09 Federation abuse | Relayed blocks run the full write gate; peers are pinned and listed; a relayed post for a channel never seen created is refused. Encrypted and restricted channels do not federate yet | Partial |
| AB-02 Botnet proof-of-work | Server rate limits per DID and address; proof-of-work for unseen DIDs, off by default. The nameserver rate-limits its v0.0.2 binding endpoints, without proof-of-work | Partial |
| AB-03 Relay and bridge quota abuse | The per-DID rate limit applies to every block's author, whichever ingress carried it. There is no limit per peer or per bridge yet | Partial |
| SC-02 Dependency substitution | Release artifacts are checksummed and signed; `install.sh` verifies both and fails closed. Builds are not reproducible | Partial |
| SC-03 Wasm runtime zero-day | The server executes only its canonical module, checked against a Wasm feature allowlist, and never encrypted content | Partial |
| PV-02 Receipt linkage | Receipts for encrypted content carry no render hash | Partial |
| TM-01 Clock-skewed farms | A block whose clock runs too far ahead of the server's is refused, and the bound is signed in the welcome | Partial |

Still open or accepted in this release, among others: OP-04 (metadata), OP-06 (omission and
reordering), OP-10 and AB-05 (Sybil resistance), AB-06 (provable abuse in encrypted channels),
TM-02 (author-set timestamps order history), and every NS and GV entry. The register lists them
all.
